target: tracker.sh supersede — an uncheckable citation leaves dependents unmet
cmd:
mkdir -p factory/specs; printf -- '---
id: 001
title: dependent
status: specd
depends_on: 002
---
body
' > factory/specs/001-a.md; printf -- '---
id: 002
title: dep
status: built
---
body
' > factory/specs/002-b.md; source "$PLUGIN_ROOT/scripts/lib/tracker.sh"; tracker_supersede factory/specs/002-b.md me no-such-ref-xyz 'landed by hand' >/dev/null 2>&1; if CLAIMED=$(tracker_claim specd building loop 2>/dev/null); then EC=0; else EC=$?; fi; jq -n --argjson ec "$EC" --arg s2 "$(_tracker_field factory/specs/002-b.md status)" --arg by "$(_tracker_field factory/specs/002-b.md superseded_by)" --arg s1 "$(_tracker_field factory/specs/001-a.md status)" --arg unmet "$(_tracker_unmet factory/specs/001-a.md)" '{ec: $ec, s2: $s2, by: $by, s1: $s1, unmet: $unmet}'
_note: the headline hazard. Marking a spec superseded when the work did NOT land recreates the field failure in tracker.sh's header — dependents building against a base missing their dependency. The status is still recorded (the claim may be true but uncheckable from here) but it unblocks nobody. Paired with 065, which proves a real citation DOES unblock, so this is not just 'supersede never works'.
